claims.text: Changing substrate temperature and deposition rate can tune film grain size.
Changing deposition parameters can tune defect density and interfacial strain.
Grain size, defect density, and interfacial strain govern the balance between magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in low-field cycles.
The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films have an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
Microstructural heterogeneities act as distributed nucleation sites during the magnetostructural transition.
A more homogeneous grain-size distribution smooths the magnetostructural transition.
Lower defect density smooths the magnetostructural transition.
Smoothing the transition through microstructural control reduces hysteresis.
Hysteresis can be reduced by microstructural control while retaining a sizable magnetic entropy change.
Optimized deposition will produce a broader but still robust magnetocaloric entropy-change peak relative to the baseline.
Optimized deposition will lower hysteretic losses relative to the baseline.
Optimized deposition will improve the surface-to-volume ratio and thereby facilitate rapid thermal exchange.
Microstructural control will make the transition less abrupt and less first-order-like by modifying nucleation and growth dynamics.
Standard unoptimized as-deposited films typically exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Standard unoptimized as-deposited films have a lower surface-to-volume ratio than optimized films.
The proposed relationship holds only over a microstructural range that preserves the magnetocaloric response while reducing hysteresis.
Excessive microstructural refinement can impair magnetic ordering.
The proposed microstructure-response relationship may not apply to arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons.
